name: pl-pharmacy-ozempic
description: Ring round Polish pharmacies for Ozempic 2 mg. One question, thirty seconds, next number.
goal:
Find out whether this pharmacy has Ozempic 2 mg (semaglutide, 2 mg pen) in stock right now.

Open with that and nothing else: whether they have Ozempic 2 mg. No name, no explanation of who is calling, no preamble.

If they say yes, that is the whole call — confirm you heard 2 mg and not another strength, note it and thank them.

If they say no, ask ONE thing: is it simply out at the moment, or is 2 mg unavailable in general — nobody has it, they cannot order it. One sentence.

Only if they say 2 mg is unavailable in general, ask one last question: the client holds a Polish prescription written for 2 mg, so would they dispense 1 mg against that 2 mg prescription? Ask it once, take whatever answer comes, and do not press, do not argue, and do not ask them to check with a pharmacist or a doctor. A plain "no" or "that depends on the doctor" is a complete answer.

Do not give the client's name, do not leave a phone number, do not ask them to hold or reserve anything, and do not ask them to call back.

ozempic_2mg_in_stock.description: Do they have Ozempic 2 mg on the shelf right now? This is the whole point of the call — ask it first.

availability.description: Whether 2 mg is in stock, merely out at the moment, or not to be had at all (nobody has it, cannot be ordered). Only ask if the answer to the first question was no.

ozempic_1mg_in_stock.description: Whether they have the 1 mg pen instead. Only relevant once 2 mg turns out to be unavailable.

would_dispense_1mg_on_2mg_prescription.description: Whether they would dispense 1 mg against a Polish prescription written for 2 mg. Ask once, take the answer as given, never push.

notes.description: Anything else worth knowing in one line — when they expect a delivery, that they can order it, that another branch has it.
